result:
I have comprehensive, well-sourced coverage across all three questions — including the authoritative OpenAI CI/CD auth guide, the new Codex access tokens, `--device-auth`, the SSH-tunnel recipes, a self-refreshing CI template, and the bridging tools. Here is the deliverable.

---

# COMMUNITY HEADLESS RECIPES — Codex CLI under ChatGPT sign-in (2025–2026)

**Bottom line up front:** Running `codex exec` non-interactively under a ChatGPT (OAuth) sign-in instead of a pay-as-you-go API key **is proven and works**, but OpenAI explicitly positions it as an *advanced / not-recommended-default* path (they steer automation to API keys). There are now **four** distinct working approaches, in rough order of cleanliness: (1) `codex login --device-auth`, (2) seed-and-persist the `~/.codex/auth.json` token file, (3) SSH-port-forward the OAuth callback (port **1455**), and (4) — Business/Enterprise only — the brand-new **Codex access tokens** (`CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, shipped 5 May 2026), which is the only truly browserless *first-class* ChatGPT-auth path. The single biggest gotcha is **token portability/refresh**: `auth.json` is copyable, but two machines sharing one copy will rotate each other's refresh token and break auth.

---

## 1. Concrete working setups (are there proven recipes? — Yes)

### Recipe A — `codex login --device-auth` (device-code flow) — *cleanest headless path*
No port forwarding, no browser on the box. CLI prints a URL + one-time code; you authorize from any browser on any device; the CLI and OpenAI's servers exchange the token.
```bash
# on the headless/remote host (over plain SSH, no -L needed):
codex login --device-auth
# → visit the printed URL on your phone/laptop, enter the code
codex exec --full-auto "run the tests and fix failures"
```
- **Prerequisite gotcha:** a workspace/account owner must first **enable "Device Code Authorization" in ChatGPT security settings**, or the auth page rejects the request.
- Official confirmation: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth (device-auth is documented as the preferred headless method).
- Real-world walkthrough (remote Mac over Tailscale + OpenClaw): https://www.vibesparking.com/en/blog/tools/openclaw/2026-04-05-openclaw-codex-remote-setup/
- **Battle-tested: Medium-High.** Documented officially and reproduced in blogs, but relatively new and gated behind the ChatGPT-settings toggle. Note some older third-party clients still claim "OpenAI has no public device-auth" (e.g. https://github.com/MadAppGang/claudish/issues/94) — that's now outdated for the *official* CLI.

### Recipe B — Seed the token file `~/.codex/auth.json` (copy between machines) — *official fallback*
Log in once on a machine with a browser, then move the JSON.
```bash
# machine WITH a browser:
codex login                       # writes ~/.codex/auth.json
# move it:
ssh user@remote 'mkdir -p ~/.codex'
scp ~/.codex/auth.json user@remote:~/.codex/auth.json
ssh user@remote 'chmod 600 ~/.codex/auth.json'
# Docker variant:
docker exec CT mkdir -p "$HOME/.codex"
docker cp ~/.codex/auth.json CT:"$HOME/.codex/auth.json"
```
Many users report you can literally paste the file's contents into `~/.codex/auth.json` on the target, `chmod 0600`, and run — no SSH forwarding (verified on Codex v0.44.0).
- Official docs: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth  and the dedicated CI guide below.
- Community confirmations in the tracking issue: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3820
- **Windows path:** `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json` (https://www.lineserve.net/guides/authenticating-codex-cli-on-a-remote-linux-server-from-windows)
- **Battle-tested: High** (widely reproduced), but see the refresh/portability caveats in §2.

### Recipe C — SSH port-forward the OAuth callback (port 1455) — *most widely documented*
The default `codex login` spins up a local callback server on **`localhost:1455`**; tunnel that port so your local browser's redirect reaches the remote CLI.
```bash
# from your LOCAL machine (keep this session open):
ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 user@remote-server
# then, in that same session on the remote:
codex login          # paste the printed auth.openai.com URL into your local browser
```
- Canonical writeups (all independently arrive at port 1455 + `-L`):
  - https://blog.codekunda.com/posts/codex-cli-headless-vps/ (also covers `--full-auto` and a "shell out to codex" pattern)
  - https://michaelbommarito.com/wiki/tools/openai-cli-remote-oauth/ (Sept 2025; `~/.ssh/config` `LocalForward`, alternate-port trick)
  - https://www.lineserve.net/guides/authenticating-codex-cli-on-a-remote-linux-server-from-windows (Windows→Linux)
  - PuTTY-specific: https://medium.com/@rviragh/exact-steps-to-start-using-chatgpt-codex-on-a-remote-linux-server-from-windows-with-putty-january-c329f11a21c9
  - **Automation script:** `codertesla/codex-remote-login` — zero-dependency bash that opens an ephemeral tunnel, triggers remote `codex login`, and tears down: https://github.com/codertesla/codex-remote-login
- **Pitfalls (from the blogs):** `lsof -i :1455` if login hangs; "State mismatch" = don't reuse an old auth URL (`pkill -f codex` first); keep the tunnel open *before* starting login (OAuth is time-limited). One source (codeongrass) mistakenly shows a reverse `-R` tunnel — **the correct direction is `-L`**; every other source agrees.
- **Battle-tested: High** for interactive first-login; but it's a one-time human step, not truly non-interactive.

### Recipe D — Official CI/CD pattern: seed-if-missing + persist the *refreshed* auth.json
This is OpenAI's own documented "run as your Codex account" recipe: **https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth/ci-cd-auth** (redirect target: learn.chatgpt.com). Also see the non-interactive doc: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode
- Model: *seed `auth.json` once → run `codex exec` normally → Codex refreshes the file in place → keep the refreshed file for next run.* There is **no separate refresh command**; any normal run refreshes a stale session.
- Force file-backed storage (not OS keyring) so it's portable: `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"` in `config.toml`.
- **Self-hosted persistent runner** (simplest): keep a persistent `CODEX_HOME`; seed from the secret *only if the file is missing* (overwriting every run throws away the refreshed tokens):
```yaml
- name: Bootstrap auth.json if needed
  env: { CODEX_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.CODEX_AUTH_JSON }} }
  run: |
    export CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"; mkdir -p "$CODEX_HOME"; chmod 700 "$CODEX_HOME"
    [ -f "$CODEX_HOME/auth.json" ] || { printf '%s' "$CODEX_AUTH_JSON" > "$CODEX_HOME/auth.json"; chmod 600 "$CODEX_HOME/auth.json"; }
- name: Run Codex
  run: codex exec --json "Reply with the single word OK." >/dev/null
```
- **Ephemeral runner (GitHub-hosted):** restore `auth.json` from secret → run → **write the refreshed file back** to secure storage (`if: always()`). Health check with `jq '{auth_mode,last_refresh,has_access_token:...}' auth.json`.
- **Battle-tested: High** — this is first-party documentation with copy-paste YAML. Caveat: officially "advanced, private repos only, not the recommended default."

### Recipe E — Codex access tokens (`CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`) — *Business/Enterprise, truly browserless*
Shipped **5 May 2026**. Workspace members mint a long-lived token; no browser, no `auth.json` file needed.
```bash
export CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN="<access-token>"
codex exec --json --sandbox workspace-write "run tests, fix failures, commit the fix"
```
```yaml
# GitHub Actions
- run: npm install -g @openai/codex@0.130.0
- env: { CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN }} }
  run: codex exec --sandbox workspace-write -o report.json "audit dependencies"
```
- Requires a ChatGPT **Business/Enterprise** workspace; owner enables "Allow members to use Codex Local" + "Codex access tokens" (RBAC-assignable). Billing rolls up under the ChatGPT subscription; workspace RBAC + compliance logs apply; **Fast mode** available (API keys can't use it). If admins push `forced_login_method = "chatgpt"`, this becomes the *only* headless option.
- Sources: official CI guide (above) + deep writeup https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/05/14/codex-access-tokens-enterprise-ci-cd-workspace-authentication-non-interactive/ and https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/codex-exec-ci-headless-guide
- **Battle-tested: Medium** (very new; Enterprise-gated so fewer public reports), but it is the *sanctioned* answer to "ChatGPT auth without a browser."

### Recipe F — `codex-session-primer` (self-refreshing encrypted auth in a private repo)
Concrete community CI template: encrypts `auth.json` → `auth.json.enc` (sops + age) committed to a **private** repo; a scheduled workflow decrypts it, runs a cheap `codex exec` on `gpt-5.4-mini` to trigger refresh, re-encrypts, and amends+force-pushes-with-lease so the next run stays logged in.
- https://github.com/VIEWVIEWVIEW/codex-session-primer  (uses `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"`; recommends `codex login --device-auth` to seed on headless).
- Explicit warning: never run concurrently (race → stale `auth.json`).
- **Battle-tested: Low-Medium** (single-author template, clever but self-described as fragile).

---

## 2. Reported gotchas

**Session refresh in headless**
- `codex exec` reuses saved auth by default and **auto-refreshes** a stale session on the next run; you don't call a refresh API yourself (official CI doc).
- Access-token lifetime is short: reports say the cached OAuth access token goes stale after **~8 days** (developersdigest) to **~10 days** (codekunda); the **refresh token** lasts weeks-to-months. On `401`, or after the refresh token is revoked/expired, you must **re-seed** from a fresh `codex login`.
- Community friction (issue #3820): *"you have to log in again after a while, breaking automation… Codex is unusable in CI/CD on a subscription. They are pushing you to use OPENAI_API_KEY."* Tracking issue: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3820 (closed in favor of **#2798**).

**Portability of the sign-in session across machines**
- `auth.json` is copyable, **but** OpenAI is explicit: *"Use one `auth.json` per runner or per serialized workflow stream. Do not share the same file across concurrent jobs or multiple machines."* Two machines on one copy will **rotate each other's tokens** and break auth (the codex-session-primer race warning is the same failure).
- **Keyring vs file store:** newer Codex may store creds in the OS keyring, not a flat file. Force portability with `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"` before copying.
- **macOS Keychain child-process trap:** when Codex (specifically Zed's `codex-acp` Rust binary) is spawned as a **detached child process** by an orchestrator, it can't reach the macOS Keychain "Codex Safe Storage" without a GUI session → `"Authentication required"` *even though `codex login status` is valid*. Workaround was to set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (defeating the ChatGPT-auth goal). https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp/issues/310  — relevant to any orchestrator that spawns Codex as a subprocess on macOS.

**`codex login` needing a browser**
- Default flow *requires* a browser reachable at `localhost:1455`; on a headless box the callback silently fails ("connection refused"/"Bad Request"). Solutions are Recipes A/B/C. Historically there was **no** device flow (that's what #3820/#2798 asked for); `--device-auth` is the resolution but needs the ChatGPT-settings toggle.

**exec sandbox / approval flags** (from config keys issue https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2760 and docs)
- `codex exec --full-auto` (auto-approve safe ops) · `--json` / `-o file` / `--output-schema` for machine-readable output.
- `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access` ; `--ask-for-approval/-a` and `approval_policy = "never"|"untrusted"|"on-failure"|"on-request"`.
- `disable_response_storage = true` for ZDR accounts. `preferred_auth_method = "apikey"|"chatgpt"` (added 2025-08-18) picks which to use when both exist.
- **Security note (official):** don't set `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`CODEX_API_KEY` as a *job-level* env var where repo-controlled code runs; scope it to the single `codex exec`. On **Windows** runners the official action needs `safety-strategy: unsafe` (no native sandbox).

**Model refusal under ChatGPT auth (surprisingly common)**
- With ChatGPT-account auth, calling `gpt-5-codex` / `gpt-5.1-codex` / `gpt-5.3-codex` returns **HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"** — you must use the account's allowed model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`). Breaks orchestrators that hardcode a `-codex` model default. Sources: https://github.com/tuannvm/codex-mcp-server/issues/192 and https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/ntm/issues/154

**Mixed-auth contamination with third-party proxies**
- After `codex login`, a stray ChatGPT OAuth token in `auth.json` (`auth_mode:"chatgpt"`) can get sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` to a third-party/proxy endpoint → `INVALID_API_KEY`. Set `requires_openai_auth=false` + explicit `env_key`. Sources: https://github.com/wei-shaw/sub2api/issues/2614 , https://github.com/saladday/cc-switch-cli/issues/328

## 3. Tooling that bridges Codex's ChatGPT-session auth into agent frameworks

| Tool | What it bridges | ChatGPT-auth support | Battle-tested |
|---|---|---|---|
| **openai/codex-action@v1** (official) — https://github.com/openai/codex-action | Runs `codex exec` in GitHub Actions; installs CLI + Responses-API proxy | API-key-centric (proxy needs `openai-api-key`); ChatGPT-auth only via the seed-`auth.json` CI pattern (Recipe D) | **High** (first-party) |
| **icoretech/codex-action** (+ `codex-docker`) — https://github.com/icoretech/codex-action | Non-interactive Codex in GH Actions, containerized | **Yes** — `codex_config` accepts a **base64-encoded `auth.json`** from a prior device-auth session; handles auto-refresh | Medium |
| **codertesla/codex-remote-login** — https://github.com/codertesla/codex-remote-login | One-command ephemeral SSH tunnel to complete `codex login` on a remote host | Yes (automates Recipe C) | Medium |
| **ndycode/codex-multi-auth** (npm) — https://github.com/ndycode/codex-multi-auth | Multi-account ChatGPT OAuth manager for the *official* CLI; account switch/health/rotation; `login --device-auth`; JSON diagnostics (`report --live --json`) | **Yes**, native OAuth focus + device-auth for headless | Medium |
| **circlemouth/codex-wrapper** — https://github.com/circlemouth/codex-wrapper | FastAPI server exposing an **OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`** backed by the Codex CLI | Yes — auth happens in the CLI (OAuth or key); wrapper inherits it | Low-Medium |
| **mr-tomahawk/codex-cli-mcp-tool** — https://github.com/mr-tomahawk/codex-cli-mcp-tool | **MCP server** so Claude Code (or any MCP host) drives Codex; explicitly pitched as "use your $20 ChatGPT sub's GPT-5 inside Claude Code" | Yes (inherits CLI login) | Low-Medium |
| **tuannvm/codex-mcp-server** — https://github.com/tuannvm/codex-mcp-server | MCP bridge for Codex | Yes, but hit the **model-400 gotcha** under ChatGPT auth (#192) | Medium |
| **zed-industries/codex-acp** — https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp | ACP adapter (Zed/other ACP hosts drive Codex) | Yes, but **child-process Keychain trap** on macOS (#310) | Medium |
| **Dicklesworthstone/ntm** — https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/ntm | Multi-agent orchestrator that spawns Codex + Claude Code (`ntm spawn proj --cod=1 --cc=2`) | Yes (inherits CLI login); had to fix hostile `-codex` model default for ChatGPT-billed users (#154) | Medium |
| **OpenClaw / moltbot / thepopebot** | Orchestrators adding an `openai-codex` provider in **oauth mode**, reading the token from `~/.codex/` | Partial — works if pre-logged-in; open request for **non-interactive** OAuth setup: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47750 | Low (in-progress) |

**Recurring theme for orchestrators:** none inject the OAuth session programmatically — they all rely on the CLI already being logged in (`~/.codex/auth.json` present). The "one command to non-interactively establish ChatGPT OAuth" gap is still open (#47750, #2798); today you bootstrap with Recipe A/B/D/E, then the framework just shells out to `codex`.

---

## Confidence / battle-tested summary
- **Highest-confidence, sanctioned:** Recipe D (official seed-and-persist CI) + Recipe E (Codex access tokens, Enterprise). Both are first-party documented at developers.openai.com/codex/auth/ci-cd-auth.
- **Highest-confidence, community:** Recipe C (SSH-tunnel port 1455) — reproduced by 6+ independent 2025-2026 writeups; Recipe B (copy `auth.json`) — confirmed in the official docs and issue threads.
- **Emerging:** Recipe A (`--device-auth`) — official but new and settings-gated; Recipe F (self-refresh template) — clever but fragile.
- **Overarching caveat every source repeats:** OpenAI's *recommended* automation path is an **API key**, not ChatGPT sign-in. ChatGPT-auth headless works but is treated as advanced, trusted-private-infra only, and carries the token-refresh/portability fragility above.

**Primary sources:** learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth · developers.openai.com/codex/auth/ci-cd-auth · learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode · developers.openai.com/codex/github-action · github.com/openai/codex/issues/3820 (+ #2798, #2760) · github.com/openai/codex-action · github.com/icoretech/codex-action · github.com/VIEWVIEWVIEW/codex-session-primer · github.com/codertesla/codex-remote-login · github.com/ndycode/codex-multi-auth · github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp/issues/310 · github.com/tuannvm/codex-mcp-server/issues/192 · github.com/dicklesworthstone/ntm/issues/154 · blog.codekunda.com/posts/codex-cli-headless-vps · michaelbommarito.com/wiki/tools/openai-cli-remote-oauth · vibesparking.com/en/blog/tools/openclaw/2026-04-05-openclaw-codex-remote-setup · codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/05/14/... · developersdigest.tech/blog/codex-exec-ci-headless-guide · lineserve.net/guides/authenticating-codex-cli-on-a-remote-linux-server-from-windows

CODEX SIGN-IN — OFFICIAL

**Scope:** OpenAI Codex CLI (open-source Rust CLI, `openai/codex`), auth model as of the 2025→mid-2026 docs. Primary sources are OpenAI's own docs (now served at `learn.chatgpt.com`, 308-redirected from `developers.openai.com/codex/*`) and the `openai/codex` GitHub repo. Community blogs are flagged as secondary.

---

## HEADLINE ANSWER (yes/no)

**Can programmatic / agent / headless Codex use the ChatGPT-account session instead of an API key?**
**YES.** All Codex entry points — interactive `codex`, non-interactive `codex exec`, and Codex-as-MCP-server (`codex mcp-server` / app-server) — share one cached login at `~/.codex/auth.json`. If that cache holds a ChatGPT sign-in, every entry point runs on it; **an API key is not required.** *(Confidence: HIGH.)*

**Caveats:** (a) OpenAI *recommends* API keys as the default for automation/CI, not because ChatGPT auth won't work but for provisioning/rotation simplicity and safety. (b) The *initial* ChatGPT sign-in needs a browser **somewhere** — on a truly browserless box you either seed `auth.json` from a machine where you logged in, use device-code login (`codex login --device-auth`, beta), or use an enterprise access token. *(Confidence: HIGH.)*

---

## 1. ChatGPT sign-in flow (`codex login`) and on-disk storage

**Flow.** Running `codex login` (or first-launch of `codex`) presents two paths: **"Sign in with ChatGPT"** (subscription access — Plus/Pro/Team/Business/Enterprise) vs **"Provide your own API key"** (usage-based). ChatGPT sign-in *"opens a browser window. After you sign in, the browser returns your credentials to Codex."* It is a standard OAuth loopback: the browser redirects back to a local callback that Codex is listening on. *(Confidence: HIGH — [learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth).)*

**Login sub-commands / flags:**
- `codex login` — interactive; opens browser for ChatGPT, or menu-select API key. *(HIGH)*
- `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key` — pipe an API key via stdin (current form; older/alt form `codex login --api-key <key>`). *(HIGH; older form per [issue #3286](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3286).)*
- `codex login --device-auth` — device-code sign-in, **labeled beta**, browserless. *(HIGH — [learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth).)*
- `printenv CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN | codex login --with-access-token` — enterprise access token (Business/Enterprise only). *(HIGH)*
- `codex logout` / TUI `/logout` — deletes the cached login. *(HIGH)*

**Storage location.** Codex writes the session to **`~/.codex/auth.json`** — *"a plaintext file at `~/.codex/auth.json` or in your OS-specific credential store."* The directory is `$CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`, same dir as `config.toml`). The file holds the OAuth token bundle (access token + refresh token + id token) — docs say *"Treat `~/.codex/auth.json` like a password: it contains access tokens."* The **CLI and IDE extension share the same cached login.** *(Confidence: HIGH — [learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth); [ci-cd-auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth).)*

**Storage backend is configurable** via `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" | "keyring" | "auto"` (default `file` = the plaintext `auth.json`; `keyring` = OS keychain). *(Confidence: HIGH — [config-reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference); [example-config.md @rust-v0.63.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.63.0/docs/example-config.md).)* The ChatGPT OAuth endpoint is overridable via `chatgpt_base_url` (default `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/`). *(HIGH — same source.)*

---

## 2. Non-interactive / headless — ChatGPT session vs. required API key

**`codex exec` (non-interactive mode):** *"`codex exec` reuses saved CLI authentication by default."* So it uses whatever is in `~/.codex/auth.json`, **including a ChatGPT session.** For a one-shot key override, `CODEX_API_KEY` is read **only** by `codex exec`. *(Confidence: HIGH — [non-interactive-mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode).)*

**Explicit official support for running as your ChatGPT account in CI/CD** exists — a dedicated page *"Maintain Codex account auth in CI/CD (advanced)"* covers running `codex exec` *"with a Codex user account instead of an API key … users who need ChatGPT/Codex rate limits instead of API key usage."* So programmatic use **does not require an API key.** OpenAI still frames API keys as the recommended default for automation. *(Confidence: HIGH — [ci-cd-auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth); [non-interactive-mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode).)*

**Codex as an MCP server / app-server:** run via **`codex mcp-server`** (alias `codex-mcp-server`; the app-server binary powers rich clients like the VS Code extension). This is *"experimental,"* uses MCP over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0), and loads the same `Config`/`$CODEX_HOME`; its OpenAI auth therefore comes from the **same shared `~/.codex/auth.json`** — it exposes `account/read`, `getAuthStatus`, `account/login/*` RPCs over that cache. So a Codex MCP/app-server also runs on the ChatGPT session when that's what's cached. *(Confidence: HIGH by shared-auth architecture + [codex_mcp_interface.md](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/docs/codex_mcp_interface.md), [app-server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server). No single doc sentence states "`codex mcp-server` reuses `auth.json`" as bluntly as the `codex exec` line does — that specific phrasing is UNVERIFIED, but the mechanism is confirmed.)*

> **Do not confuse two different "chatgpt auth" settings.** `mcp_servers.<id>.auth = "chatgpt"` (and the underlying `use_chatgpt_auth` flag) controls whether Codex forwards *your ChatGPT session as a bearer credential to a downstream, same-origin, first-party ChatGPT-hosted MCP server* — it is **not** how Codex authenticates *itself* to OpenAI. *(HIGH — [config-reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), [developers.openai.com/codex/mcp](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp), [commit 4c0706e #29733](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/4c0706e24a290f89c40d99b92912367c63fe273d).)*

### Config key that forces the ChatGPT session — IMPORTANT VERSION SPLIT

- **CURRENT (Codex CLI ≥ 0.35.0): `forced_login_method`** — type **`chatgpt | api`**, *"Restrict Codex to a specific authentication method."* Set in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  # ~/.codex/config.toml
  forced_login_method = "chatgpt"   # forces ChatGPT session; blocks API-key auth
  ```
  Note the value is **`api`**, not `apikey`. *(Confidence: HIGH — [config-reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference); [example-config.md @rust-v0.63.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.63.0/docs/example-config.md).)*

- **LEGACY / REMOVED: `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt" | "apikey"`** — this is the exact key named in the task. It was real (added ~Aug 18 2025) and was set as `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt"` in `~/.codex/config.toml` (or ad-hoc `codex --config preferred_auth_method="chatgpt"`) to force the subscription session. **It was eliminated in Codex CLI 0.35.0.** Per the maintainer: *"The `preferred_auth_method` config option is eliminated. ## 3. Session lifetime & refresh (incl. headless refresh)

- **Access tokens are short-lived and auto-refreshed during use:** *"For sign in with ChatGPT sessions, Codex refreshes tokens automatically during use before they expire, so active sessions usually continue without requiring another browser login."* Proactive refresh is implemented ([PR #23546 "Refresh near-expiry ChatGPT access tokens before requests"](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/23546)), plus a 401 refresh-and-retry fallback. *(Confidence: HIGH — [learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth), [ci-cd-auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth).)*

- **Official staleness threshold ≈ 8 days:** *"if `last_refresh` is older than about 8 days, Codex refreshes the token bundle before the run continues."* Meaning: as long as Codex runs at least roughly every ~8 days it silently rolls the token bundle forward; the refresh rewrites `auth.json` in place. *(Confidence: HIGH for the ~8-day figure as the refresh trigger — [ci-cd-auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth). Secondary corroboration: [developersdigest](https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/codex-exec-ci-headless-guide), [danielvaughan KB](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/01/codex-cli-authentication-flows-credential-management/).)*

- **Refresh works WITHOUT a browser.** Refresh uses the stored refresh token, no browser. On a headless runner the documented pattern is: *"Create `auth.json` once on a trusted machine with `codex login`" → "Put that file on the runner" → let any normal run refresh it → "Keep the refreshed `auth.json` for the next run."* Critical gotcha: *"If you rewrite the file from the original secret on every run, you throw away the refreshed tokens that Codex just wrote"* — persist the file Codex updated, don't re-seed from the stale secret. The home dir must be writable and not shared across untrusted jobs. *(Confidence: HIGH — [ci-cd-auth](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth).)*

- **Hard upper bound (when re-login IS forced):** If `auth.json` sits untouched long enough that the **refresh token itself** expires (or you `/logout`, or an admin revokes), you must re-authenticate via browser/device-auth. The exact maximum idle lifetime of the refresh token is **not published officially** — the ~8 days is the *proactive-refresh trigger*, not a proven hard expiry ceiling. **Mark the precise refresh-token max lifetime UNVERIFIED.** *(Confidence: MEDIUM.)*

- **Enterprise access tokens differ:** admin-set finite expiration (community example ~30 days); a resumed run that outlives the token is not auto-refreshed and needs re-auth. This is the access-token path, distinct from the ChatGPT OAuth session above. *(Confidence: MEDIUM — official [access-tokens](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens) + secondary [danielvaughan KB](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/05/14/codex-access-tokens-enterprise-ci-cd-workspace-authentication-non-interactive/).)*

# LIMITS & TOS — ChatGPT-subscription sign-in with OpenAI Codex CLI in automated / headless contexts (2025–2026)

**Scope caveat (read first):** This space moved fast and OpenAI did a major pricing overhaul on **April 2, 2026**, switching Codex from *per-message* limits to *token/credit-based* limits ([OpenAI rate card](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106-codex-rate-card)). Published caps are **dynamic ranges, not fixed numbers**, and they shifted across model generations (GPT‑5.5 → GPT‑5.6). Treat all specific message counts as *rough, time-sensitive* figures. Confidence graded per claim; `[UNVERIFIED]` = could not confirm against a primary/authoritative source.

## 1. Usage limits — subscription vs. API billing

**Two different auth routes hit two different backends** (MED–HIGH — [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/), [OpenAI auth docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)):
- **ChatGPT sign-in (subscription):** routes through `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`; draws from **included plan limits + credits**. This backend endpoint is **not a documented public API** and "can change without notice."
- **API-key sign-in:** uses standard `api.openai.com/v1/` endpoints; **billed per-token at standard API rates**, through your OpenAI Platform org.

### Subscription-side limits (ChatGPT sign-in)

Codex is **bundled into every ChatGPT plan** — there is no separate Codex subscription (HIGH). Tiers: Free $0, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo (choose **5x** or **20x** limits), Business (~$20/user/mo), Enterprise/Edu/Health/Gov custom ([pricing](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing), [rate card](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106-codex-rate-card)).

- **5-hour rolling window is the primary limit** (HIGH). *"All limits apply to a 5-hour rolling window, not a daily or monthly cap"* — you can burn the whole window in one intense session ([UI Bakery](https://uibakery.io/blog/openai-codex-pricing), [community #1378768](https://community.openai.com/t/understanding-the-new-codex-limit-system-after-the-april-9-update/1378768)).
- **A separate WEEKLY cap stacks on top of the 5-hour window** (MED–HIGH). It *"resets on a rolling 7-day calendar from your first message of the week."* You can hit one limit while still having room in the other ([routerpark](https://routerpark.com/blog/chatgpt-codex-limits), [ofox.ai](https://ofox.ai/blog/codex-weekly-limit-drained-2026/)). OpenAI's own help center confirms the framing but does **not publish exact weekly numbers** — `[UNVERIFIED: precise weekly caps]`.
- **CLI, web, and IDE share the same window** (HIGH) — a heavy CLI/agent session competes with your web usage for one allowance ([discussion #2251](https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/2251)).
- **Codex now counts toward a pooled "agentic usage limit"** shared with ChatGPT for Excel and Workspace Agents (MED — OpenAI help center, *"Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan"*). This matters for automation: parallel agentic features drain the *same* bucket.

**Rough per-tier message caps** (MED — ranges vary by task size/model and by date):

| Tier | Rough caps per 5-hour window |
|---|---|
| **Plus $20** | GPT‑5.5 ≈ **15–80 msgs**; GPT‑5.4 ≈ 20–100; GPT‑5.4‑mini ≈ 60–350. (Later GPT‑5.6 table: Sol 15–90, Terra 20–110, Luna 50–280.) |
| **Pro 5x ($100)** | ≈ **5× Plus** (e.g. GPT‑5.5 ≈ 75–400) |
| **Pro 20x** | ≈ **20× Plus** (e.g. GPT‑5.5 ≈ 300–1,600) |
| **Business** | ≈ same as Plus, **per seat** |

Sources: [morphllm](https://www.morphllm.com/codex-pricing), [eesel](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/codex-pricing), [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/). Note: OpenAI framed these as *"the number of messages varies based on size and complexity of your coding tasks"* (help center) — the ranges are inherently fuzzy. A Pro "**temporary 2× boost**" was noted as ending **May 31, 2026** (MED — [simplemetrics](https://simplemetrics.xyz/chatgpt-codex-limits-2026/)). Post‑Apr‑2026, spend is also expressible in **credits**: *"a typical Codex task using GPT‑5.5 may consume 5–45 credits"*; real-world cost cited at **~$100–200/developer/month** ([rate card](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106-codex-rate-card)). Plus/Pro users can **buy overflow credits** when a limit is hit.

### API-billing side (API-key sign-in)
- **No 5-hour or weekly windows.** Pure usage-based token billing at standard API rates + your org's normal API rate limits (RPM/TPM by usage tier). E.g. **gpt‑5.3‑codex ≈ $1.75 / 1M input, $14.00 / 1M output** (MED — [morphllm](https://www.morphllm.com/codex-pricing)).
- This is OpenAI's **recommended route for CI / headless / automation** (see §2).

### Models: subscription-only vs. API-only (MED — this is the counterintuitive part)
- **Newest models land on the subscription (ChatGPT-auth) route FIRST.** At launch (**Apr 23, 2026**), **GPT‑5.5 was available *only* through ChatGPT subscription auth in Codex surfaces (App/CLI/IDE) — NOT via API keys** ([webscraft](https://webscraft.org/blog/gpt55-v-codex-scho-zminilos-dlya-rozrobnikiv-u-2026?lang=en); Simon Willison literally called it *"the semi-official Codex backdoor API"* — [simonwillison.net](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Apr/23/gpt-5-5/)).
- **API-key mode gets newer models on a delay** and **strips cloud features** — no GitHub integration, no Slack integration, no Codex cloud ([morphllm](https://www.morphllm.com/codex-pricing); [OpenAI auth docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth): *"some features that rely on ChatGPT workspace access or cloud services are limited or unavailable"*).
- Code review runs on **GPT‑5.3‑Codex** (rate card). Model availability on the subscription side can **change without notice** — e.g. [issue #25839](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25839): *"GPT‑5.3‑Codex removed for ChatGPT subscription accounts despite being listed as supported."*

**Net:** subscription buys you *newest models + cloud features + windowed "free" usage*; API buys you *stability, predictable billing, no windows, but delayed models + no cloud integrations*.

## 2. Does OpenAI's policy permit driving the subscription session from automation / multi-agent / CI?

**This is genuinely ambiguous — there is a documented tension between an explicit ToS clause and a semi-official "use it anywhere" endorsement. There is no clean written permission for unattended CI.**

### Signals that it's PERMITTED / tolerated
- **Codex CLI is Apache‑2.0 licensed; forking/modifying is explicitly fine.** OpenAI maintainer @etraut‑openai: *"The codex CLI sources are licensed under a permissive Apache license, and you're welcome to fork the repo and make modifications"* — but he added he is *"an engineer, not a lawyer"* and pointed to the Terms for the ToS question ([discussion #8338](https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/8338)). **Confidence HIGH; but note it does NOT resolve the ToS question.**
- **OpenAI DevEx lead Romain Huet, publicly (primary source, HIGH):** *"We want people to be able to use Codex, and their ChatGPT subscription, wherever they like! That means in the app, in the terminal, but also in JetBrains, Xcode, OpenCode, Pi, and now Claude Code. That's why Codex CLI and Codex app server are open source too!"* ([x.com/romainhuet, Apr 2026](https://x.com/romainhuet/status/2038699202834841962)). OpenAI even shipped a plugin to *"call Codex from Claude Code with your ChatGPT subscription"* ([x.com](https://x.com/romainhuet/status/2038677236304245087)).
  - **Critical read:** this endorses using your subscription across **interactive third-party *clients*** — it is **not** a statement about **unattended CI / multi-account pooling / server automation**. Do not over-read it.

### Signals that it's RESTRICTED
- **OpenAI Terms of Use, "What you cannot do" (verbatim, HIGH — [row-terms](https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/)):**
  - *"Automatically or programmatically extract data or Output."*
  - *"Interfere with or disrupt our Services, including circumvent any rate limits or restrictions or bypass any protective measures or safety mitigations we put on our Services."*
  - *"Modify, copy, lease, sell or distribute any of our Services."*
  - *"Attempt to or assist anyone to reverse engineer, decompile or discover the source code or underlying components of our Services…"*
  - The *"automatically or programmatically extract… Output"* clause is the one an aggressive reviewer could read as covering headless/agent automation, though "using the official CLI as intended" vs. "programmatic extraction" is a **genuinely unsettled line** `[UNVERIFIED: OpenAI has not publicly drawn it]`.
- **Account pooling / credential sharing across a proxy is the clear red line.** *"The semi-official endorsement… applies to individual, personal use of your own subscription. Account pooling and credential sharing sit in a greyer area"* ([danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/)). Combined with the ToS "circumvent rate limits" clause, rotating multiple subscription accounts to dodge windows is the highest-risk pattern.
- **OpenAI's own documented guidance steers automation to API keys:** the auth docs distinguish subscription sign-in ("subscription access") from API-key ("usage-based access"), and third-party guidance is consistent: *"if the work needs CI, SDK, headless automation, or explicit token billing, use an API key"* ([LaoZhang](https://blog.laozhang.ai/en/posts/codex-api-key-vs-subscription)).

### Documented risk of throttling / account action (LOW confidence on causation — `[UNVERIFIED]`)
- A wave of **unexplained ChatGPT Pro / Codex account bans and suspensions** was reported **May–July 2026** on OpenAI's own community forum, several tied to heavy Codex use, plan-switching, or suspected account-sharing ("shared-egress theory"): [banned 18-month subscriber](https://community.openai.com/t/codex-chatgpt-pro-account-banned-with-no-warning-no-explanation-18-month-subscriber/1381906), [switching plans → bans](https://community.openai.com/t/switching-subscription-plans-can-lead-to-account-bans/1385430), [false suspensions ↔ quota anomalies](https://community.openai.com/t/recent-false-suspensions-of-paid-users-may-be-connected-to-the-codex-quota-anomalies/1385096).
- **Causation is not confirmed** — many reporters claim no policy violation, appeals often went unanswered, and some look like false positives from quota bugs. But the practical signal for an automation user is real: **heavy, machine-like, or multi-account subscription usage is a plausible ban-risk vector, and OpenAI's abuse enforcement is opaque and offers little recourse.**

**Bottom line (§2):** Single-user, single-account, interactive-style automation of *your own* subscription via the official CLI is **tolerated in practice** (Huet's stance + Apache license). But it is **not contractually blessed for unattended CI**, the ToS contains a clause that cuts against programmatic use and explicitly forbids circumventing rate limits, and **multi-account pooling/proxying is a clear violation risk**. For anything production/CI, OpenAI's structural intent is **use an API key**.

## 3. Reliability in headless — session expiry, refresh, 401/403

**The dominant, well-documented failure is login/auth in browserless environments — not mid-run token expiry.**

- **The OAuth callback uses `localhost`, so "Sign in with ChatGPT" cannot complete on SSH boxes, containers, CI runners, WSL, Codespaces, tmux** (HIGH — multiple issues): [#2798](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2798), [#3820](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3820), [#1976](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/1976), [#2763](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2763)/[#8692](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/8692) ("login stuck on 'Sign in with ChatGPT' screen"). Symptom: hangs at "Press Enter to continue," no device code, no copyable URL.
- **Workaround = device-code auth (beta):** `codex login --device-auth`, or select it in the interactive login UI (HIGH).
- **BUT device-code auth can be disabled at the workspace level by an admin — and then headless login fails *entirely*, even for authorized users who work fine in a GUI** ([#9253](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/9253)): *"Codex CLI forces Device Code authentication in headless environments. If Device Code authentication is disabled at the workspace level, login fails entirely."* This is a hard blocker for Enterprise/Team-tenant automation. **Confidence HIGH.**
- **Copying the cached credential/token file from an interactive machine to the headless one works** and lets Codex authenticate without a browser (MED — [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/); the practical de-facto method for CI on subscription auth).
- **Mid-run token refresh is claimed to be robust:** *"Tokens refresh automatically during active sessions, so long-running CI jobs or automation scripts rarely hit expiry"* (MED — single-source, [danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/)). `[UNVERIFIED against an OpenAI primary source]` — and it's counterweighted by the undocumented-endpoint risk below.
- **Structural fragility for automation (MED–HIGH):**
  - The subscription backend (`/backend-api/codex/responses`) is **undocumented and "can change without notice"** — no stability/SLA guarantee for headless pipelines ([danielvaughan](https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/codex-subscription-api-programmatic-access-gpt-5-5-chatgpt-plan/)).
  - **Models can be pulled from the subscription route without notice** mid-workflow ([#25839](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25839)).
  - Proxy sensitivity: ChatGPT-login Codex is **unstable behind a SOCKS5 proxy**, recovers with HTTP(S)_PROXY ([#20844](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20844)) — relevant to locked-down CI networks.
- **401/403 specifically:** I did **not** find a confirmed widespread "mid-run 401 refresh-loop" bug report; the documented 401/403-class pain is concentrated at **initial login/refresh in headless + workspace-admin gating**, not steady-state session drops. `[UNVERIFIED: no primary confirmation of a recurring mid-run 401/403 failure mode]`.

**Reliability verdict:** ChatGPT-subscription auth is **usable but brittle** headless — getting logged in is the hard part (device-auth + possible admin gating), the backend is an undocumented moving target, and enforcement/model changes can surprise a pipeline. For unattended reliability, **API-key auth is materially more robust** (documented endpoints, no window resets, no OAuth-callback problem), at the cost of losing cloud features and newest-model day-one access.

# Codex ChatGPT sign-in vs API key (headless/agent) — Feasibility

## Verdict

**PARTIAL (works with caveats) — technically fully supported, operationally brittle, contractually grey.** All three investigators agree the mechanism works: every Codex entry point (`codex`, `codex exec`, `codex mcp-server`/app-server) shares one cached login at `~/.codex/auth.json`, and if that holds a ChatGPT sign-in, an API key is not required (Inv. 1, HIGH). The caveats are real and independent: headless *initial* login needs a workaround, subscription usage is capped by 5-hour + weekly windows, the backend is undocumented and can change without notice, and OpenAI's own guidance steers automation to API keys.

## How the sign-in works (official)

- **Two auth paths.** `codex login` offers "Sign in with ChatGPT" (subscription: Plus/Pro/Team/Business/Enterprise, routes through `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`) vs "Provide your own API key" (usage-based, `api.openai.com/v1/`). ChatGPT sign-in is a standard OAuth loopback — browser redirects to a local callback (port **1455**), which is why it fails on browserless boxes (Inv. 1 HIGH; Inv. 2/3 HIGH).
- **Where the session lives.** `~/.codex/auth.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json`), a plaintext OAuth bundle (access + refresh + id token) by default, or the OS keychain. Directory is `$CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`). Backend is configurable: `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" | "keyring" | "auto"`. The **CLI, IDE extension, and MCP/app-server all share this one file** (Inv. 1, HIGH).
- **`codex exec` and app-server honor the ChatGPT session.** Docs state `codex exec` "reuses saved CLI authentication by default" (Inv. 1, HIGH). `codex mcp-server` shares the same `Config`/`$CODEX_HOME`, so it also runs on the cached ChatGPT session — confirmed by shared-auth architecture, though **no single doc sentence states this as bluntly for mcp-server as for exec (doc-phrasing UNVERIFIED)** (Inv. 1).
- **Config key to force the ChatGPT session — CONFLICT between investigators, flagged:**
  - **Inv. 1 (HIGH, issue #3286):** the task's named key `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt"` was **removed in Codex CLI 0.35.0** and is now **ignored**; the replacement is **`forced_login_method = "chatgpt"`** (note the API value is `api`, not `apikey`). Post-0.35, "the last login method is always assumed to be your preferred method."
  - **Inv. 3** still lists `preferred_auth_method = "apikey"|"chatgpt"` (added 2025-08-18) as a live key "picks which to use when both exist," without noting its removal.
  - **Reconciliation:** Inv. 1 explicitly traces the timeline (added Aug 2025 → removed 0.35.0) and is the more specific source; Inv. 3's mention appears to draw from the older issue (#2760). **Treat `forced_login_method` as current; assume `preferred_auth_method` is legacy/inert on any recent Codex.** Verify against your installed version.
- **Session refresh.** Proactive: Codex refreshes the token bundle if `last_refresh` is older than **~8 days**, using the stored refresh token — **no browser needed** — and rewrites `auth.json` in place, plus a 401 refresh-and-retry fallback (Inv. 1 HIGH; Inv. 3 corroborates ~8–10 day access-token staleness, refresh token lasting weeks-to-months). **Refresh-token hard maximum lifetime is UNVERIFIED** (not published; ~8 days is the refresh *trigger*, not a proven expiry ceiling).

## Steps to switch to the ChatGPT sign-in (Windows)

1. **Interactive first login (box with a browser):**
   ```
   codex login          # choose "Sign in with ChatGPT"
   ```
   Writes `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json`.
2. **Headless/no-browser first login — pick one:**
   - `codex login --device-auth` (beta; prints URL + code to authorize from any device). **Prerequisite:** a workspace owner must enable "Device Code Authorization" in ChatGPT security settings, or it fails (Inv. 3 HIGH; Inv. 2 flags admin-disable as a hard blocker, issue #9253).
   - **Seed the file:** run `codex login` on a machine with a browser, copy `auth.json` to `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json` on the target, restrict perms. Works and is the de-facto CI method (Inv. 3 HIGH).
   - SSH-forward port 1455 (`ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 …`) for a one-time remote login (Inv. 3, community, HIGH).
3. **Force file-backed, portable storage** in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
   ```toml
   cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"
   forced_login_method = "chatgpt"   # current key; blocks silent API-key fallback
   ```
   (Do **not** rely on `preferred_auth_method` — see conflict above.)
4. **Run non-interactively:** `codex exec --full-auto "…"` (or `--json` / `-o file` for machine-readable output). It reuses `auth.json` automatically.
5. **What an agent-orchestration wrapper must do so it does *not* force an API key:**
   - **Do not set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY`** in the job/process env — `CODEX_API_KEY` is read by `codex exec` and overrides the cached session; a stray key also causes mixed-auth contamination with proxies (Inv. 1, Inv. 3).
   - **Persist the *refreshed* `auth.json`, never re-seed from the stale secret each run** — overwriting throws away the rolled-forward tokens Codex just wrote and breaks auth (Inv. 1, Inv. 3, both HIGH).
   - **One `auth.json` per runner / serialized stream** — two machines sharing one copy rotate each other's refresh token and break auth (Inv. 3 HIGH).
   - **Don't hardcode a `-codex` model default:** under ChatGPT auth, `gpt-5-codex`/`gpt-5.1-codex`/`gpt-5.3-codex` can return HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"; use the account-allowed model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`) (Inv. 3, MED).
   - macOS-only trap (not Windows): a detached child Codex can't reach the Keychain → "Authentication required"; forces file-store or a key (Inv. 3).

## Limitations & risks

- **Rate limits (subscription vs API).** Subscription is capped by a **5-hour rolling window (primary) + a stacked weekly cap**, and **CLI/web/IDE share the same window** — a heavy agent run competes with your interactive usage (Inv. 2, HIGH). Post-April-2026 repricing moved to token/credits; per-tier message counts are **dynamic ranges, and exact weekly numbers are UNVERIFIED** (not published). API-key mode has **no windows** — pure per-token billing — which is OpenAI's recommended automation path (Inv. 2, HIGH).
- **Model access.** Newest models land on the **subscription route first** (GPT-5.5 was subscription-only at launch — "the semi-official Codex backdoor API"); API mode gets new models on a **delay and strips cloud features** (GitHub/Slack/Codex cloud). Conversely, **models can be pulled from the subscription route without notice** mid-workflow (Inv. 2, MED–HIGH; issue #25839).
- **ToS on automated subscription use — genuinely ambiguous, no clean written permission for unattended CI (Inv. 2).** *For:* Codex CLI is Apache-2.0 (fork/modify fine), and OpenAI DevEx lead Romain Huet publicly endorsed using "Codex, and their ChatGPT subscription, wherever they like" (HIGH) — **but that endorsement is scoped to interactive third-party *clients*, not unattended CI or multi-account pooling.** *Against:* the Terms forbid "automatically or programmatically extract … Output" and "circumvent any rate limits," which an aggressive reading covers (whether it's *intended* to cover official-CLI automation is **UNVERIFIED** — OpenAI hasn't drawn the line). **Multi-account pooling / credential sharing to dodge windows is the clear red line.** A May–July 2026 wave of Codex/Pro account bans is documented, but **causation is UNVERIFIED** (several look like quota-bug false positives).
- **Headless refresh reliability.** Usable but brittle: **getting logged in is the hard part** (localhost-callback failure → device-auth, which an admin can disable workspace-wide = hard blocker; issue #9253 HIGH). Mid-run refresh is claimed robust but is **single-sourced (danielvaughan) and UNVERIFIED against an OpenAI primary source** (Inv. 2/3). The backend endpoint is **undocumented with no SLA** and unstable behind SOCKS5 proxies. No confirmed recurring mid-run 401/403 failure mode was found (**UNVERIFIED**).
- **Enterprise escape hatch.** ChatGPT **Business/Enterprise** can mint `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (shipped May 2026) — truly browserless, RBAC-governed, the *sanctioned* headless answer — but requires an Enterprise workspace and admin enablement (Inv. 1/3). Not available to individual Plus/Pro.

## Recommendation

**Hybrid — ChatGPT-session primary, API-key fallback — for this user's profile.** The user's use case (Codex as a parallel agent alongside Claude, quality > cost, **budget-paced across weekly windows**) maps directly onto the subscription model: the 5-hour + weekly caps *are* the exact pacing cadence, and subscription buys newest-model-first access plus "free" windowed usage that the per-token API doesn't. Single-user, single-account, interactive-style automation of *your own* subscription via the official CLI is tolerated in practice (Huet + Apache license), and this profile is far closer to that than to unattended multi-account CI.

Keep an **API key wired as fallback** (via `CODEX_API_KEY` on the specific `codex exec` invocation, exec-only) for the failure modes the findings make concrete: window exhaustion, a model getting pulled from the subscription route, or refresh breaking on a headless runner. This preserves budget-pacing benefits while covering the brittleness.

**Hard constraints:** (1) run **one account per session** — do **not** pool multiple ChatGPT accounts through a proxy (the clear ToS red line + the plausible ban vector); (2) **persist the refreshed `auth.json`, never re-seed from the stale secret**; (3) migrate any config off `preferred_auth_method` to `forced_login_method` after verifying your installed version. *Do not switch fully off the API key* — the undocumented backend, model-pull risk, and unverified refresh robustness make subscription-only automation too fragile for a load-bearing parallel agent.
